column11: Pesachim 120a: ‘What is the reason that it is optional to eat matza on the first six days of Passover as well as the seventh? The seventh day of Passover is something that was included in a generalization but was explicitly singled out to teach. According to the rules of exegesis, it was intended to teach not just about itself but about the entire generalization. In other words, the seventh day of Passover was initially included in the verse: “You shall eat matzot for seven days” (Exodus 12:15), but was excluded from this generalization by the verse: “Six days you shall eat matzot.” In accordance with the above principle, the halakha of the seventh day applies to all the other days of Passover as well.…’ Context and connection to Ohr Zarua LaTzadik: In Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, Novellae, On Mitzvot 3, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Pesachim 120a) to illuminate his exposition here (“And if you argue that the verse regarding Matzah was required to establish it as an obligation on the first night (Pesachim 120a), then with circumcision too the repetition served a specific halakhic derivation; and...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the hidden light of Torah, the spiritual root of the letters and mitzvot, and the halakhic-aggadic synthesis developed in Ohr Zarua LaTzadik.
